1. (Currently amended) A lamp comprised of an at least substantially hollow columnar body, a plurality of light emitting diodes disposed on said columnar body, a plurality of fins disposed on said columnar body, a base member disposed at a first end of the columnar body and providing a means for electrical connection, and an electronics module disposed within the columnar body and in electrical communication with the base member, __wherein said plurality of light emitting diodes are disposed on side faces of the columnar body and said plurality of fins are disposed on corners of the columnar body.__

2. (Currently amended) The lamp of claim 1 wherein a second end of said columnar body is open __to permit air flow through the hollow columnar body__.

3. (Currently amended) The lamp of claim 1 further including __a plurality of__ light dispersing optic __elements, each__ overlapping __a respective one of__ said diodes.

4. (Currently amended) The lamp of claim 3 wherein __each said__ optic element includes a phosphor material.

5. (Previously presented) The lamp of claim 1 wherein said diodes are substantially evenly spaced radially around the columnar body.

6. (Currently amended) The lamp of claim 5 wherein said fins are substantially equally disposed between said diodes, __one fin residing on each corner of the columnar body and one diode residing on each face of the columnar body__.

7. (Previously presented) The lamp of claim 7 wherein said columnar body comprises one of a tetragon, pentagon, hexagon, heptagon, octagon, nonagon, decagon, hendecagon, or dodecagon in cross-section.

8. (Previously presented) The lamp of claim 8 wherein at least one diode resides on each face of said columnar body.

9. (Previously presented) The lamp of claim 9 wherein one fin resides on each corner of said columnar body.

10. (Currently amended) The lamp of claim 9 wherein a single diode resides on each face __of said columnar body__.

11. (Previously presented) The lamp of claim 1 wherein said columnar body and said fins are comprised of a material having a thermal conductivity greater than 100 W/ mK.

12. (Currently amended) The lamp of claim 9 including a single optic element __disposed between each adjacent fin and__ overlapping said diode.

13. (Previously presented) The lamp of claim 1 wherein said base member comprises an Edison screw base or a wedge base.

14. (Currently amended) The lamp of claim 1 wherein said electronics module comprises a printed circuit board including circuitry for converting AC to DC current __disposed within the hollow columnar body between the base member and the second end of the columnar body__.

15. (Currently amended) The lamp of claim 3 wherein said optic element preferentially directs light substantially perpendicular to an elongated axis of the columnar body __through a sidewardly facing light output surface__.

16. (Currently amended) A lamp comprising an elongated hollow polygonal body comprised of a material having a thermal conductivity greater than 100 W/ mK, a fin extending radially from each corner of said body, a light emitting diode mounted to each side of said body, a screw or wedge base connector closing a first end of said body, a second end of said body being open __to permit air flow through said body__, an electronics module disposed within said body in electrical communication with said connector and said light emitting diodes, said lamp having a general A19 outline.

17. (Currently amended) A method of manufacturing a lamp comprising extruding an elongated hollow __polygonal__ body, said body comprised of a material having a thermal conductivity greater than 100 W/ mK, cutting said body to a predetermined length, attaching at least one light emitting diode to said body __on a side face thereof__, and providing electrical circuitry suitable for powering said light emitting diode.

18. (Previously presented) The method of claim 17 wherein said material has a thermal conductivity greater than about 150 W/ mK.

19. (Previously presented) The method of claim 17 wherein said body includes a plurality of integral radially extending fins.

20. (Currently amended) The method of claim 17 wherein said body has substantially straight side walls __defining said polygonal body__.
